Figure 5.12 Image Description 
The chemical structures of a saturated, monounsaturated, and two polyunsaturated fats 
are shown. The saturated fatty acid shows no C=C double bonds. The monounsaturated fatty 
acid shows one C=C double bond. One polyunsaturated fatty acid shows two C=C double 
bonds and another polyunsaturated fatty acid shows three C=C double bonds. 
Triglycerides in food contain a mixture of saturated, monounsaturated, and polyunsaturated 
fatty acids, but some foods are better sources of these types of fatty acids than others (Figure 5.13). 
For example, coconut oil is very high in saturated fat, but it still contains some monounsaturated and 
polyunsaturated fatty acids. Peanut oil is often thought of as a good source of monounsaturated fat, 
because that is the predominant fatty acid in the oil, but peanut oil also contains a fair amount of 
polyunsaturated fatty acids and even some saturated fatty acids.
